1377: def _llm_check_spec_update(proj_dir, work_dir, idx, fqn, lang_key, comment_prefix,
1378:                            developer_intent, spec_block, info_block, callee_names, source):
1379:     """
1380:     Ask the LLM whether a function's [SPEC] (and, if so, its [INFO]) block must change to
1381:     reflect developer_intent, and return the parsed decision.
1382: 
1383:     The prompt inlines the entire function source, its current [SPEC]/[INFO] blocks, and the
1384:     developer intent, so it needs no repository file access and is issued as a direct LLM
1385:     call (via _llm_select_json) rather than an opencode run. idx is used only to label the
1386:     traced exchange.
1387: 
1388:     Returns the parsed result dict — keys: "spec_updated" (bool), "new_spec" (str),
1389:     "info_updated" (bool), "new_info" (str), "updated_callees" (list[str]) — or None when
1390:     the LLM produced nothing usable.
1391:     """
1392:     callee_hint = ", ".join(sorted(callee_names)) if callee_names else "(none)"
1393:     if not callee_names:
1394:         info_section = "This function has no callees, so there is no [INFO] block to maintain.\n\n"
1395:     elif info_block is not None:
1396:         info_section = (
1397:             "## Current [INFO] block (the expected specs of the callees this function depends on)\n\n"
1398:             f"{info_block}\n\n"
1399:             "NOTE: a modification may have changed which callees this function calls, so this "
1400:             f"block may be missing entries for some current callees ({callee_hint}) or contain "
1401:             "entries for callees no longer called.\n\n"
1402:         )
1403:     else:
1404:         info_section = (
1405:             "This function currently has no [INFO] block, but a modification may have made it "
1406:             f"call other functions, so it now has callees ({callee_hint}); a new [INFO] block "
1407:             "may need to be created for them.\n\n"
1408:         )
1409: 
1410:     knowledge_section = _domain_knowledge_prompt_section(work_dir)
1411: 
1412:     prompt_content = (
1413:         "# Update Function Specification\n\n"
1414:         "A modification is being applied to a codebase to achieve the developer intent "
1415:         "below. Decide whether this function's behavioral specification must change to "
1416:         "reflect that intent.\n\n"
1417:         f"- Function fully-qualified name: `{fqn}` (language: `{lang_key}`).\n"
1418:         f"- Comment prefix for this language: `{comment_prefix}`.\n"
1419:         f"- Known callees of this function: {callee_hint}.\n\n"
1420:         "## Developer intent\n\n"
1421:         f"{developer_intent}\n\n"
1422:         f"{knowledge_section}"
1423:         "## Current function source\n\n"
1424:         f"```{lang_key}\n{source.strip()}\n```\n\n"
1425:         "## Current [SPEC] block (this function's own behavioral specification)\n\n"
1426:         f"{spec_block}\n\n"
1427:         f"{info_section}"
1428:         "## Steps\n\n"
1429:         "1. Decide whether the [SPEC] block still correctly and completely describes the "
1430:         "function's behavior after the intended modification. If it remains correct, no "
1431:         "update is needed.\n"
1432:         "2. If it must change, produce the COMPLETE replacement [SPEC] block — the "
1433:         "`[SPEC]` ... `[SPEC]` block only, markers included, every line prefixed with "
1434:         f"`{comment_prefix}`, and NO source code.\n"
1435:         "3. ONLY if you updated the [SPEC] block AND this function has callees: bring the "
1436:         f"[INFO] block into line with this function's CURRENT callees ({callee_hint}). That "
1437:         "means: (a) keep entries whose recorded expectation still matches the callee's role, "
1438:         "(b) ADD an entry for any current callee not yet recorded (e.g. one the modification "
1439:         "introduced), (c) DROP entries for callees this function no longer calls, and (d) "
1440:         "revise any entry whose expected spec must change as a consequence of the new [SPEC]. "
1441:         "If any of (a)-(d) changes the block, produce the COMPLETE replacement [INFO] block "
1442:         f"(the `[INFO]` ... `[INFO]` block only, markers included, lines prefixed with "
1443:         f"`{comment_prefix}`) and list the names of the callees whose expected spec you added "
1444:         "or changed.\n"
1445:         "4. Return ONLY a JSON object with keys:\n"
1446:         '   - "spec_updated": boolean.\n'
1447:         '   - "new_spec": string — the full replacement [SPEC] block, or "" if not updated.\n'
1448:         '   - "info_updated": boolean — true when you produced a new/replacement [INFO] block.\n'
1449:         '   - "new_info": string — the full replacement [INFO] block, or "" if not updated.\n'
1450:         '   - "updated_callees": array of callee name strings whose expected spec you added or changed, or [].\n'
1451:         "   Do not include Markdown, tags, or prose outside the JSON object.\n"
1452:     )
1453: 
1454:     return _llm_select_json(
1455:         work_dir,
1456:         prompt_content,
1457:         stage="update_function_spec",
1458:         validator=_validate_spec_update,
1459:         schema_description=(
1460:             '{"spec_updated": boolean, "new_spec": string, "info_updated": boolean, '
1461:             '"new_info": string, "updated_callees": [string]}'
1462:         ),
1463:         trace_meta={"fqn": fqn, "idx": idx},
1464:     )

1525: def _collect_caller_context(fqn, callers_map, file_map, edge_aliases_map=None):
1526:     """
1527:     Gather the context an existing caller provides about fqn, mirroring the caller context
1528:     run_pipeline feeds into spec generation: each caller's own [SPEC] block and the entry in
1529:     its [INFO] block that records what the caller expects from fqn (as one of its callees).
1530: 
1531:     Returns a list of (caller_fqn, caller_spec, callee_expectation) tuples — caller_spec and
1532:     callee_expectation are None when the caller has no such block — for every caller of fqn
1533:     whose extracted-function file exists and yields at least one of the two. Callers with no
1534:     file or no usable block are skipped.
1535:     """
1536:     context = []
1537:     for caller_fqn in sorted(callers_map.get(fqn, ())):
1538:         cpath = file_map.get(caller_fqn)
1539:         if not cpath or not os.path.isfile(cpath):
1540:             continue
1541:         cpath_p = Path(cpath)
1542:         caller_spec = extract_spec_block(cpath_p)
1543:         info_block = extract_info_block(cpath_p)
1544:         aliases = ()
1545:         if edge_aliases_map:
1546:             aliases = tuple(edge_aliases_map.get(fqn, {}).get(caller_fqn, ()))
1547:         expectation = extract_callee_spec_from_info(info_block, fqn, aliases) if info_block else None
1548:         if caller_spec or expectation:
1549:             context.append((caller_fqn, caller_spec, expectation))
1550:     return context

1553: def _opencode_generate_spec(proj_dir, work_dir, idx, fqn, lang_key, comment_prefix,
1554:                             developer_intent, callee_names, source, caller_context):
1555:     """
1556:     Ask opencode to generate a brand-new [SPEC] (and, when the function has callees, [INFO])
1557:     block from scratch for a function that has no existing specification — e.g. a function
1558:     freshly added by the modification.
1559: 
1560:     Mirrors the full run's spec generation (run_pipeline Stage 6) but for a single function:
1561:     opencode reads the project's spec format rules (fm_agent/spec_prompts/system_prompt.md),
1562:     is given the same caller context the full run provides (each caller's [SPEC] block and what
1563:     that caller's [INFO] block expects from this function, in caller_context as returned by
1564:     _collect_caller_context), and produces the block(s) directly. Returns the parsed decision
1565:     in the SAME shape as _opencode_check_spec_update so the caller can splice and propagate it
1566:     identically.
1567: 
1568:     Returns the parsed result dict — keys: "spec_updated" (bool, true when a [SPEC] block was
1569:     produced), "new_spec" (str), "info_updated" (bool), "new_info" (str), "updated_callees"
1570:     (list[str]) — or None when opencode produced nothing usable.
1571:     """
1572:     result_relpath = os.path.join("fm_agent", f"spec_generate_{idx}.json")
1573:     prompt_relpath = os.path.join("fm_agent", f"spec_generate_{idx}.md")
1574: 
1575:     # Caller context (callers' own specs + what each caller's [INFO] expects from this
1576:     # function), mirroring run_pipeline's "EARLIER-LAYER CALLER SPECS" / "CALLEE EXPECTATIONS
1577:     # FROM CALLERS" sections so the generated spec satisfies what callers depend on.
1578:     caller_specs = [
1579:         (cfqn, spec) for cfqn, spec, _ in caller_context if spec
1580:     ]
1581:     caller_expectations = [
1582:         (cfqn, exp) for cfqn, _, exp in caller_context if exp
1583:     ]
1584:     caller_section = ""
1585:     if caller_specs:
1586:         caller_section += "## Specs of this function's callers\n\n"
1587:         for cfqn, spec in caller_specs:
1588:             caller_section += f"### {cfqn}\n\n{spec.strip()}\n\n"
1589:     if caller_expectations:
1590:         caller_section += (
1591:             "## What callers expect from this function (from their [INFO] blocks)\n\n"
1592:             "Your generated [SPEC] must be consistent with these expectations.\n\n"
1593:         )
1594:         for cfqn, exp in caller_expectations:
1595:             caller_section += f"### According to {cfqn}\n\n{exp.strip()}\n\n"
1596: 
1597:     callee_hint = ", ".join(sorted(callee_names)) if callee_names else "(none)"
1598:     user_knowledge_paths = list_staged_domain_knowledge_relpaths(work_dir)
1599:     if user_knowledge_paths:
1600:         user_knowledge_step = (
1601:             "2. Read these user-provided domain knowledge Markdown files and use "
1602:             "them as additional context:\n"
1603:             f"{format_domain_knowledge_bullets(user_knowledge_paths)}\n"
1604:         )
1605:         step_offset = 1
1606:     else:
1607:         user_knowledge_step = ""
1608:         step_offset = 0
1609:     info_step_number = 3 + step_offset
1610:     if callee_names:
1611:         info_step = (
1612:             f"{info_step_number}. Because this function has callees, also produce an [INFO] block recording the "
1613:             "expected behavioral spec of each callee it depends on (the `[INFO]` ... `[INFO]` "
1614:             f"block only, markers included, every line prefixed with `{comment_prefix}`), and "
1615:             "list the names of the callees you recorded.\n"
1616:         )
1617:     else:
1618:         info_step = f"{info_step_number}. This function has no callees, so produce no [INFO] block.\n"
1619: 
1620:     prompt_content = (
1621:         "# Generate Function Specification\n\n"
1622:         "A modification has been applied to a codebase to achieve the developer intent below, "
1623:         "adding a function that has no behavioral specification yet. Generate its "
1624:         "specification from scratch.\n\n"
1625:         f"- Function fully-qualified name: `{fqn}` (language: `{lang_key}`).\n"
1626:         f"- Comment prefix for this language: `{comment_prefix}`.\n"
1627:         f"- Known callees of this function: {callee_hint}.\n\n"
1628:         "## Developer intent\n\n"
1629:         f"{developer_intent}\n\n"
1630:         "## Function source\n\n"
1631:         f"```{lang_key}\n{source.strip()}\n```\n\n"
1632:         f"{caller_section}"
1633:         "## Steps\n\n"
1634:         "1. Read `fm_agent/spec_prompts/system_prompt.md` for the exact [SPEC]/[INFO] format "
1635:         "rules used by this project.\n"
1636:         f"{user_knowledge_step}"
1637:         f"{2 + step_offset}. Produce the COMPLETE [SPEC] block describing this function's behavior — the "
1638:         "`[SPEC]` ... `[SPEC]` block only, markers included, every line prefixed with "
1639:         f"`{comment_prefix}`, and NO source code.\n"
1640:         f"{info_step}"
1641:         f"{4 + step_offset}. Write your answer to `{result_relpath}` as a JSON object with keys:\n"
1642:         '   - "spec_updated": boolean — true when you produced a [SPEC] block.\n'
1643:         '   - "new_spec": string — the full [SPEC] block.\n'
1644:         '   - "info_updated": boolean — true when you produced an [INFO] block.\n'
1645:         '   - "new_info": string — the full [INFO] block, or "" if none.\n'
1646:         '   - "updated_callees": array of callee name strings recorded in [INFO], or [].\n'
1647:         "   Write ONLY that JSON file; do not modify any other project files.\n"
1648:     )
1649: 
1650:     return _opencode_select_json(
1651:         proj_dir,
1652:         work_dir,
1653:         prompt_relpath,
1654:         prompt_content,
1655:         result_relpath,
1656:         stage="generate_function_spec",
1657:         input_files=[

1665: def _update_specs_for_intent(
1666:     proj_dir,
1667:     work_dir,
1668:     developer_intent,
1669:     changed_functions,
1670:     relevant_rel_files,
1671:     extra_call_edges=None,
1672: ):
1673:     """
1674:     re-generate the [SPEC] (and dependent [INFO]) blocks of every function that is
1675:     either changed or relevant to the developer intent, propagating to callees.
1676: 
1677:     Seeds from the changed functions (added/modified) and the relevant extracted-function
1678:     files returned by collect_relevent_function_scope, then processes functions in top-down
1679:     order (callers before callees). For each function, opencode reads its current [SPEC]
1680:     block and decides whether it must change to reflect developer_intent. A function with no
1681:     existing [SPEC] block (e.g. one freshly added by the modification) instead has a spec
1682:     generated from scratch the way the full run does. If a spec is written or generated, the
1683:     new [SPEC] is written back (source untouched), and then:
1684: 
1685:       - Downward: opencode decides whether the function's own [INFO] block (the expected
1686:         specs of its callees) must change too, and any callee whose expected spec changed is
1687:         queued to have its own spec file re-checked.
1688:       - Upward: every caller's [INFO] block (which records this function as one of its
1689:         callees) is reconciled with the function's new [SPEC] so the two do not conflict
1690:         (they need not be identical).
1691: 
1692:     Returns the sorted list of extracted-function files (paths relative to the
1693:     extracted_functions dir) whose [SPEC]/[INFO] block was changed.
1694:     """
1695:     extracted_dir = os.path.join(work_dir, "extracted_functions")
1696: 
1697:     callees_map, callers_map, file_map, edge_aliases_map = _project_call_graph(
1698:         work_dir,
1699:         extra_call_edges=extra_call_edges,
1700:     )
1701: 
1702:     # Seed: functions changed in the working tree (added/modified — removed ones no longer
1703:     # exist on disk) plus functions relevant to the developer intent.
1704:     seed = set()
1705:     changed_targets = _modified_function_targets(
1706:         proj_dir, changed_functions, classes=("added", "modified")
1707:     )
1708:     seed.update(changed_targets.keys())
1709:     for rel in relevant_rel_files:
1710:         seed.add(_file_to_fqn(os.path.join(extracted_dir, rel), work_dir))
1711: 
1712:     if not seed:
1713:         logging.info("    [specs] no changed or relevant functions to update; skipping.")
1714:         return []
1715:     logging.info(
1716:         "    [specs] seeded %d function(s) for spec re-generation (%d changed, %d relevant).",
1717:         len(seed), len(changed_targets), len(relevant_rel_files),
1718:     )
1719: 
1720:     # Top-down order (callers before the callees they depend on); FQNs absent from the layer
1721:     # graph sort last, by name.
1722:     topdown = _topdown_ordered_fqns(work_dir, extra_call_edges=extra_call_edges)
1723:     order_index = {fqn: i for i, fqn in enumerate(topdown)}
1724: 
1725:     def _order_key(fqn):
1726:         return (order_index.get(fqn, len(order_index)), fqn)
1727: 
1728:     def _plan_spec_update(fqn, idx):
1729:         """
1730:         Decide fqn's new [SPEC]/[INFO] and return an apply-plan, or None to skip.
1731: 
1732:         Makes the opencode LLM call (the slow part) but performs NO file writes, so a batch of
1733:         mutually independent functions can run this concurrently. The returned plan carries the
1734:         exact file content to write plus what the serial apply phase needs for downward
1735:         propagation; None means the function does not exist, is an unsupported language, or its
1736:         spec did not change.
1737:         """
1738:         fpath = file_map.get(fqn)
1739:         if not fpath or not os.path.isfile(fpath):
1740:             return None
1741:         ext = fpath.rsplit(".", 1)[-1] if "." in os.path.basename(fpath) else ""
1742:         lang_key = EXT_TO_LANG.get(ext)
1743:         if not lang_key:
1744:             return None
1745:         lang_cfg = LANG_CONFIG[lang_key]
1746:         comment_prefix = lang_cfg["comment_prefix"]
1747:         spec_marker = lang_cfg["spec_marker"]
1748: 
1749:         with open(fpath, "r", errors="replace") as f:
1750:             content = f.read()
1751:         leading = _extract_leading_spec_comments(content, comment_prefix, spec_marker)
1752:         callee_names = sorted({c.split("::")[-1] for c in callees_map.get(fqn, ())})
1753: 
1754:         if leading is None:
1755:             # No existing specification (e.g. a freshly added, unspecced function) — generate
1756:             # one from scratch the way the full run does, rather than skipping the function.
1757:             source = content
1758:             old_spec, old_info = None, None
1759:             caller_context = _collect_caller_context(
1760:                 fqn, callers_map, file_map, edge_aliases_map
1761:             )

## Reasoning Process

The following actual behavior cannot satisfy the specification.

### Specification Claim

- Returns a list of paths, each relative to the extracted_functions/ directory, ordered by
    descending relevance to developer_intent; paths with equal relevance are ordered lexicographically
- Every returned path refers to an existing regular file under extracted_functions/
- When range is not None, the returned list has length  range
- Returns an empty list when phases.json defines no modules, or when no module is selected
    by the relevance assessment
- A module is selected when EITHER its natural-language description (as recorded in phases.json)
    is assessed as relevant to the developer intent, OR the module contains at least one source file
    whose path, relativized against proj_dir, matches a key in changed_functions
- Within each selected module, a source file is included only when its content is assessed as
    relevant to the developer intent, EXCEPT that every source file present in changed_functions
    is included unconditionally
- When the per-module file-relevance assessment cannot be obtained, every source file in that
    module is included
- Within each included source file, the set of extracted functions whose relevance scores
    (computed from heuristic signals derived from developer_intent) rank within the top of that file
    are included
- When per-file function ranking is unavailable for an included source file, every extracted
    function from that file is included
- Multiple extracted-function files mapping to the same source-level function are deduplicated,
    keeping only the occurrence with the highest relevance score

---

### Actual Behavior

Let L be the list returned by collect_relevent_function_scope. The function does not modify any of its arguments or the filesystem (it only reads files and writes logs). Under the given preconditions (proj_dir contains fm_agent/phases.json and fm_agent/extracted_functions, developer_intent is nonempty, changed_functions has the required structure, range is None or a nonnegative integer) the following holds:

If the flattened module list derived from phases.json is empty (no modules in any phase), L = [].

Otherwise, the function performs three passes:
1. Module selection: an LLM chooses a subset of modules relevant to developer_intent.
2. File selection: for each chosen module, opencode selects a subset of its source files.
3. Function selection: for each selected file, rank_functions_in_file ranks the functions and returns a list of dicts ordered by descending score. Through _extracted_files_by_method each relevant function is mapped to one or more extractedfunction file paths relative to proj_dir/fm_agent/extracted_functions. The union of these paths, ordered by the original descending scores (preserving perfile order and combining files by descending modulethenfile relevance), forms a sequence S.

If S is empty (no modules, files or functions were selected), L = [].
If range is None, L = S.
If range is a nonnegative integer, L = S[:range] (the first at most range paths).

Thus: L is a list of strings, each string is a relative path into the extracted_functions directory, and L is sorted by decreasing relevance to developer_intent. The list is empty exactly when the selection process produces no results.

## Trigger Condition

Specification requires that a module is selected when it contains at least one source file whose relative path matches a key in changed_functions, even if its description is not assessed as relevant. The code performs only an LLMbased relevance assessment on module descriptions and does not incorporate the changed_functions criterion. In the counterexample, the module with an irrelevant description contains a file present in changed_functions, so it must be selected, but the code omits it, yielding an empty list instead of the required nonempty result.

## How to trigger the bug

The bug claim asserts that `collect_relevent_function_scope` does NOT incorporate the `changed_functions` criterion in module selection. However, inspection of the source code at `src/incremental_reasoner.py` lines 1158-1162 reveals the `relevant_modules` list comprehension explicitly includes an `or any(sf.replace("\\", "/") in changed_source_rels ...)` clause that selects modules containing files present in `changed_functions`, regardless of LLM assessment. The probe confirms this logic operates correctly.

### Inputs

| Parameter | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| selected_keys (LLM selection) | `set()` (empty — LLM selected no modules) |
| changed_source_rels | `{"src/utils/helper.py", "src/main.c"}` |
| modules[0] (core_module) | `{"name": "core_module", "source_files": ["src/core/engine.py", "src/core/alloc.py"]}` — no files in changed_source_rels |
| modules[1] (util_module) | `{"name": "util_module", "source_files": ["src/utils/helper.py", "src/utils/format.py"]}` — "src/utils/helper.py" IS in changed_source_rels |

### Expected (spec-correct) Output

`["util_module"]` — the module containing a file in `changed_functions` must be selected even though LLM found nothing relevant.

### Actual (buggy) Output

`["util_module"]` — the code DOES correctly select the module via the `changed_functions` criterion. The bug claim is not reproduced.

## Probe Script

```python
"""Probe: validate whether collect_relevent_function_scope incorporates the
changed_functions criterion in module selection.

Spec claim: A module is selected when EITHER its description is assessed as
relevant by LLM, OR the module contains at least one source file whose
relativized path matches a key in changed_functions.

Bug claim: "The code performs only an LLM-based relevance assessment on module
descriptions and does not incorporate the changed_functions criterion."

This probe tests the exact filtering expression from the source code
(src/incremental_reasoner.py line ~1161) to verify the claim.
"""

import sys
import os

# --- The exact logic under test, extracted verbatim from the source ---

def _filter_relevant_modules(modules, selected_keys, changed_source_rels):
    """Verbatim reproduction of the filtering logic at lines 1158-1162 of
    src/incremental_reasoner.py."""
    return [
        (phase_num, module)
        for phase_num, module in modules
        if (phase_num, module.get("name")) in selected_keys
        or any(
            sf.replace("\\", "/") in changed_source_rels
            for sf in module.get("source_files", [])
        )
    ]


# --- Test case: LLM selects NO modules, but a module has a changed file ---

def main():
    # Simulate: LLM returned empty selection (no modules assessed as relevant)
    selected_keys = set()

    # Simulate: changed_functions maps an absolute path to a source file;
    # after relativization and normalization, it becomes "src/utils/helper.py"
    changed_source_rels = {"src/utils/helper.py", "src/main.c"}

    # Simulate: phases.json defines two modules
    modules = [
        (1, {
            "name": "core_module",
            "description": "Core infrastructure module",
            "source_files": ["src/core/engine.py", "src/core/alloc.py"],
        }),
        (2, {
            "name": "util_module",
            "description": "Utility helpers module",
            "source_files": ["src/utils/helper.py", "src/utils/format.py"],
        }),
    ]

    # Apply the filtering logic
    relevant = _filter_relevant_modules(modules, selected_keys, changed_source_rels)

    # Spec says: "util_module" must be selected because its source_file
    # "src/utils/helper.py" matches a key in changed_source_rels, even though
    # selected_keys is empty (LLM found nothing relevant).
    #
    # Bug claim says: code does NOT incorporate the changed_functions criterion,
    # so relevant would be []. But the code DOES have the `or any(...)` clause,
    # so relevant should be [(2, util_module)].

    module_names = [m.get("name") for _, m in relevant]
    expected = ["util_module"]

    if module_names == expected:
        print(
            "NOT CONFIRMED — changed_functions criterion IS incorporated: "
            f"selected modules={module_names}, expected={expected}"
        )
    elif module_names == []:
        print(
            "CONFIRMED — changed_functions criterion NOT incorporated: "
            "empty result when util_module should have been selected via "
            "changed_functions"
        )
    else:
        print(
            f"UNEXPECTED — modules selected: {module_names}, "
            f"expected: {expected}"
        )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    try:
        main()
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"ERROR: {e}")
        sys.exit(1)
```
